solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chaotic electronic pop is rank

indicators.note: chaos is disorder, so the following letters are thrown out of their order

parts.note: taken as written; it doubles as fodder

explanation.surface: A sneer at messy synthesised pop music as rank, that is, offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective meaning foul, but it is a noun: a grade in the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A police inspector is a grade in the British police hierarchy, above sergeant, so it is a rank.

clue.text: Reduce two to one on a timely basis

definitions.text: Reduce two to one on a timely basis

parts.note: surface reading: shrink a pair to a single, or shorten betting odds
setter's reading: turn the hour hand from two o'clock back to one, as when the clocks change in autumn

explanation.surface: Sounds like cutting odds or halving something on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two to one' suggests betting odds; here it is the time, changed by an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning the hands back an hour at the end of summer time moves the reading from two o'clock to one.

clue.text: Femme fatale sorely needing clothing dons garland

indicators.note: the word is left stripped, wanting its outer covering of first and last letters
to don is to put on, so one piece wears the other around it

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A seductive woman, in sore need of clothes, puts on a flower wreath.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed word goes inside the garland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the Rhine siren who lured boatmen to their deaths, hence any dangerous temptress.

clue.text: Pleasant dance briefly advanced in reverse sequence

indicators.note: kept short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a conga is a line dance

indicators.note: going in the opposite direction, so the letters are read back to front
one piece placed in another

parts.note: a line is a sequence or row
A is the abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: A dance figure performed backwards in a pleasant manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The dance is cut short, then A sits inside LINE and the whole is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenial describes agreeable company or surroundings, a near synonym of pleasant.

clue.text: Perfect example of croupier's running commentary?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a model of perfection
second meaning: what a dealer at the card table might keep saying

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, 'I deal', and it becomes the card dealer's commentary; the question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard of perfection; split in two it is a dealer's announcement.

clue.text: Bank statement preceding dodgy cash withdrawal?

definitions.text: Bank statement preceding dodgy cash withdrawal

parts.note: surface reading: a printed account summary from the bank
setter's reading: what a robber says inside the bank just before taking the money

explanation.surface: Sounds like a statement arriving before a suspicious withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank statement' is a document in the surface but words spoken in a bank in the cryptic reading.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the classic demand a holdup man makes to raise hands before robbing the bank.

clue.text: Evacuation of English army's top soldiers in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the letters run the other way
the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A military evacuation: English troops pulling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuation' looks military, but it is the medical sense of emptying the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is a procedure that flushes out the bowel, so it is an evacuation in the medical sense.

clue.text: Gets canines, perhaps from leader of hunt beset by support group from the south

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the bottom means upwards, back to front
to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides
the leader is the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A hound pack scene: the lead hunter surrounded by supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The group is reversed and the hunt's first letter goes inside it, after the support.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby teethes when its teeth come through, canines being one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: In which you'd find users/authors get alternative?

definitions.text: In which you'd find users/authors get alternative

indicators.note: an alternative version offers a different arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Where writers and readers look up an alternative word.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a thesaurus is where writers get alternative words.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget's is the classic thesaurus, a reference book of synonyms consulted for other words.

clue.text: Recent works by European dramatist

indicators.note: works suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: New plays by a playwright from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a Roman comic playwright of the second century BC.

clue.text: I caught aquatic bird going over floating mass

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: going over suggests turning over, so the bird's name is read backwards

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher catches a water bird flying over drifting ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is a large mass of ice adrift at sea.

clue.text: Split orchestra, one left downsized by 90%?

indicators.note: cutting a Roman numeral to a tenth of its value swaps it for a smaller numeral

parts.note: the Hallé is a Manchester orchestra
L for left, also the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: An orchestra splits up, with one player leaving after drastic downsizing.
explanation.walkthrough: L is fifty in Roman numerals; ninety percent off leaves five, which is V, so one L in the orchestra's name becomes V.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to split it into two equal parts.

clue.text: Pound store ruined instantly

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling
shot means worn out or wrecked

explanation.surface: A discount pound shop wrecked in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound store' reads as a bargain shop, but it splits into a currency abbreviation and a named store.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a shot is an idiom for at once, without any delay.

clue.text: Jerk is decked by felon's stick

indicators.note: decked suggests surrounded and adorned on the outside

parts.note: crim is slang for a criminal
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A jerk floored by a criminal wielding a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decked' looks like knocked down; it means enclosed. 'Stick' is a noun meaning harsh comment.
explanation.definitionFit: To get stick is British slang for receiving abuse or censure, so stick means criticism.

clue.text: After time among Arctic people, setter's understood immediately

indicators.note: being among people places one inside the group

parts.note: the setter says I've, short for I have

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter, having spent time among the Inuit, grasps things at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's stands for 'setter has', the setter saying I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuitive knowledge is grasped instinctively without reasoning, so understood immediately.

clue.text: Composer's catalogue picked up

indicators.note: picked up as by ear or a microphone, so it is what the word sounds like

explanation.surface: A composer's work catalogue gets acquired.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the composer to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic composer and virtuoso pianist.

clue.text: Mistress meets maker in South African town

parts.note: a lady is a mistress of the house

explanation.surface: A man's lover meets a craftsman in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladysmith is a town in KwaZulu-Natal, famous for its siege in the Boer War.

clue.text: Waste from Cornish river

parts.note: of can mean from, as in 'of noble birth'
the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: Pollution coming out of a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-west tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal originally meant refuse, the parts cut off as waste in butchery.

clue.text: Hunter, pro, suppressing anger

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down within, so one piece encloses the other

explanation.surface: A professional hunter keeping a lid on his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' looks like a professional; it is the preposition meaning in favour of.
explanation.definitionFit: A forager searches for food, the way a hunter seeks out prey.

clue.text: Peter and David almost shuffling deck

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
shuffling mixes cards, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the name without its last letter

explanation.surface: Two men shuffling a deck of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffling deck' paints cards, but the deck is a tape deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape deck is the mechanism that plays and records tape, as is a tape drive.

clue.text: Tough guy, smooth, wanting threesome in romance

parts.note: to iron is to smooth out

indicators.note: a threesome in the middle of a word means its central three letters

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking hard man looking for a three-way romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Threesome' suggests something racy; it just picks three letters from the middle of romance.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron man is a person of great strength and endurance, a tough guy.

clue.text: British bore, chasing king and queen, that could make folk cross?

parts.note: to bore a hole is to drill it

explanation.surface: A tedious British person tailing the royal couple, enough to annoy anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' means coming after, so British bore follows the king and queen. 'Cross' looks like angry but means crossing the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The kerb drill is the British road-safety routine taught to children for crossing the street safely.

clue.text: Severe legislator once pulled up old comic

indicators.note: in a down entry, pulled up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a card is a joker or comedian

explanation.surface: A harsh lawmaker of the past rebuked an elderly comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulled up' looks like scolded; in a down clue it turns the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco was the Athenian lawgiver whose harsh code gave us the word draconian.

clue.text: Rabies rampant in grassy land

indicators.note: rampant means rearing up, which in a down entry reads the letters upward
in says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: A rabies outbreak running wild in pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rampant' looks like widespread; it is the heraldic rearing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyssa is the medical name for rabies, from the Greek for madness.

clue.text: Car manufacturer backed promo agreements

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the letters run in the reverse order

explanation.surface: A carmaker supported promotional deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like supported; it is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Skoda is a Czech motor company, now part of the Volkswagen group.

clue.text: Monetary unit of Ghana I forged, netting fine

indicators.note: netting means catching inside, so the letter is enclosed
something forged is beaten into a new shape

explanation.surface: A counterfeiter confesses to forging currency and getting fined.
explanation.definitionFit: The afghani is the currency unit of Afghanistan.

clue.text: He superficially reads second Kipling work right after setter

indicators.note: one thing placed right after another comes second, setting the order of the two pieces

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A reader skips through another Kipling book after the setter's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right after setter' puts R straight after ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A skimmer is someone who skims, reading quickly and only at the surface.

clue.text: Camera shake OK in fixed audiovisual gear?

indicators.note: fixed as in rigged or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A photographer's blurred shots are passable in the repaired equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is fodder too: its letters join the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke machines play backing music and show lyrics on screen, so they are sound-and-vision kit.
